record_identity.title: Moltbook database exposure revealed private communications and API authentication tokens

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Moltbook database exposure revealed private communications and API authentication tokens
incident_identity.date_basis: Wiz disclosed the exposure to Moltbook and published its findings on 2 February 2026; Business Insider reported them on 3 February.

summary: Security researchers found an unsecured Moltbook backend that exposed about 35,000 email addresses, thousands of private messages and approximately 1.5 million API authentication tokens with read-and-write implications.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Business Insider reports that Wiz researchers accessed the database in under three minutes and obtained full read-and-write access. The exposed authentication tokens could enable account impersonation and content manipulation. Wiz disclosed the issue, Moltbook secured it within hours, and Wiz said the research data was deleted.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence is a large-scale data and credential exposure caused by a backend security misconfiguration. The evidence does not establish that an AI model made the configuration decision or that a current VIGIL Failure Class is the right mechanism abstraction.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case shows that AI-agent platforms remain dependent on conventional application-security controls for credentials, private communications and account integrity.
assessment_boundaries: The reviewed evidence does not establish malicious exploitation beyond the security research or downstream token misuse.
Claims about development method do not by themselves establish a causal model failure.
